Tech stocks were edging higher early Friday following Thursday's out-sized advance.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Gogo ( GOGO ) advanced during Friday's pre-market, rising over 9%, after the in-flight connectivity company reiterated its FY18 revenue guidance as it is set to reach free cash flow break-even by 2020 as well as significant yearly EBITDA growth seen rising to more than $200 million in 2022. CEO Oakleigh Thorne said the recent initiatives are positioning Gogo for sustainable value creation, adding he expects to reduce cash burn at the company by over $100 million in FY19 from prior-year levels and by a further $100 million in 2020. The firm maintained its revenue target of $865 million to $935 million for 2018, in line with its prior guidance and market expectations for $885.96 million in revenue this year.
In other sector news:
+ ShiftPixy ( PIXY ) jumped over 7% in Thursday late trading after the staffing software firm issued preliminary fiscal Q3 financial results, expecting net loss of $0.06 per share for the three months ended May 31, improving a $0.11 per share net loss during the year-earlier period, as revenue more than doubled year-over-year, rising to $9.4 million from $4.6 million last year. The workforce platform company also said gross billings more than doubled over last year to $60.2 million, compared to $27.5 million for the March-to-May reporting period in 2017. The company said it expects to provide a new release date for its Q3 results as soon as possible.
- Bruker ( BRKR ) fell fractionally late Thursday after the scientific instruments and measurements company said it acquired JPK Instruments AG, a biomolecular and cellular imaging company based in Berlin, Germany. The target company also provides force measurements on single molecules, cells and tissues and generated around EUR10 million, or about $11.7 million, in annual revenue during 2017. Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
